title: Maintaining Air Quality
seo_title: Secondary 4 Chemistry: Maintaining Air Quality Worksheets (O-Level 6092 with Answers)
standard_text: Describe the composition of clean, dry air; state the sources of air pollutants such as carbon monoxide, sulfur dioxide, oxides of nitrogen, unburnt hydrocarbons, methane and ozone and describe their effects; describe the formation of acid rain and ways of reducing it, including flue gas desulfurisation; describe how catalytic converters remove pollutants; describe the importance of the ozone layer and its depletion by CFCs; describe the carbon cycle and the effect of increased greenhouse gases on global warming (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Chemistry 6092 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Chemistry worksheets on maintaining air quality: composition of air, air pollutants, acid rain, catalytic converters, the ozone layer, the carbon cycle, global warming and the haze. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Know each pollutant: source, effect, removal.
key_sub: Air: 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, 0.9% argon, 0.04% carbon dioxide.
body_html:
How to think about it

Most air pollution comes from burning fuels.

  • Carbon monoxide: incomplete combustion, toxic. Sulfur dioxide: sulfur in fuels, acid rain. Oxides of nitrogen: N₂ + O₂ in hot engines, acid rain and smog.
  • Catalytic converters turn CO, NO and hydrocarbons into CO₂, N₂ and H₂O. Flue gas desulfurisation uses CaCO₃ or CaO to remove SO₂.
  • The ozone layer absorbs UV; CFCs destroy it. Carbon dioxide and methane trap infrared radiation and cause global warming.
Example

How much oxygen is in 400 cm³ of air?

21% of 400 = 0.21 × 400

Answer: about 84 cm³

Example

2CO + 2NO → ? in a catalytic converter

C goes to CO₂, N goes to N₂

Answer: 2CO₂ + N₂

Common mistakes

  • Saying air is mostly oxygen.
  • Saying carbon dioxide causes acid rain (it is SO₂ and NO₂).
  • Saying a catalytic converter removes carbon dioxide.
  • Mixing up the ozone hole (UV) and global warming (infrared, greenhouse gases).

faq.a: Sulfur dioxide from burning fuels that contain sulfur and nitrogen dioxide from car engines dissolve in rainwater to form sulfuric and nitric acids.

faq.q: What does a catalytic converter do?
faq.a: It uses hot platinum and rhodium catalysts to change carbon monoxide, oxides of nitrogen and unburnt hydrocarbons into carbon dioxide, nitrogen and water.

faq.q: What is the difference between the ozone layer problem and global warming?
faq.a: CFCs destroy ozone, so more ultraviolet light reaches the Earth. Global warming is caused by greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide and methane trapping infrared radiation.
